findings.title: A dummy TOTP value lets a backup code bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation, so a request containing an email, a valid backupCode, an arbitrary totpCode such as "x", and an empty or incorrect password successfully authenticates. The dummy TOTP is never checked. This makes a backup code sufficient by itself rather than a replacement for the second factor. Require a verified first factor before accepting the backup code.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically
findings.body: Backup codes are checked against the user snapshot read earlier, then the entire encrypted array is overwritten with an unconditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both validate it and successfully log in. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code that was already consumed. This violates the advertised single-use guarantee and permits replay. Use locking or a conditional update against the original stored value, and authenticate only when consumption succeeds.

findings.title: Backup recovery is unavailable in the third-party 2FA flow
findings.body: A user can generate backup codes with a CAL account and subsequently link Google or SAML; the sign-in code changes their identity provider while retaining their 2FA settings and backup codes. Their subsequent 2FA challenge has totpEmail and renders ExternalTotpFooter, which has only Cancel—not the new Lost access control. Consequently twoFactorLostAccess cannot become true and the backup-code field is unreachable. The credentials provider also rejects backup-only submissions for non-CAL users because its identity-provider guards recognize only totpCode. These users cannot use their saved recovery codes after losing their authenticator.

findings.title: Finalize successful enablement on every dialog dismissal path
findings.body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, onEnable is no longer called; it is deferred to the custom backup-codes-close button. Closing the backup-code dialog through Escape or the dialog's standard close control invokes only the passed-through onOpenChange handler, so onEnable never fires even though 2FA is already enabled on the server. This breaks the callback contract and leaves consumers relying on it with stale security settings. Notify the parent on success, or ensure every dismissal path after success invokes onEnable.

findings.title: Do not override PasswordField's visibility-controlled input type
findings.body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField sets its input type from isPasswordVisible but spreads props afterward, so this explicit prop overrides the dynamic type. Clicking the new show-password control changes its icon and label but never reveals the password. Remove the explicit type prop so PasswordField can control visibility.
